evals.prompt: Design a URL shortener for 100M new URLs per day.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 opens with one question about the most consequential open decision (read/write ratio, retention or latency SLO), with a recommended answer, and waits.
expectations: The first reply asks exactly one question
The question carries a recommended answer and a reason
No design doc is written before the questions are settled
The reply does not ask for a fact the prompt already gives (100M URLs per day)

evals.prompt: Design a URL shortener for 100M new URLs per day. I am away all day: send me all your questions at once and I will answer by code.
evals.expected_output: Batch mode: one coded questionnaire Q1..Qn covering every open question whose prerequisites are settled, each with a recommended answer.
expectations: Questions are coded Q1, Q2, and so on, in a single message
There are more than 5 questions or the reply states that no more are open
Every question has a recommended answer
No question depends on the answer to another question in the same batch

evals.prompt: Design a URL shortener for 100M new URLs per day. Use your recommendation for every question and write the doc.
evals.expected_output: A design doc at docs/designs/<slug>.md with all 13 template sections, assumptions labelled, capacity arithmetic shown, a mermaid diagram, and status draft, followed by a Phase 3 review request to a reviewer from another vendor.
expectations: The doc path is under docs/designs/ with a kebab-case slug
All 13 template sections appear in order
Capacity shows the formula: 100M per day is about 1160 writes per second on average
Each assumed value is labelled Assumption:
The architecture section contains a mermaid block
Deep dives cover 2 or 3 parts, each with why it was picked
The header status is draft, not accepted
Phase 3 names a reviewer from a different vendor than the author and gives it the doc, not the conversation

evals.prompt: Let's practise a system design interview. Senior level, 45 minutes, design a rate limiter.
evals.expected_output: Interview mode: the skill states a vague prompt and asks one question at a time without recommended answers.
expectations: The reply states the prompt as an interviewer would
It asks one question and gives no recommended answer
It does not write a file under docs/designs/

evals.prompt: Rename the `userId` parameter to `accountId` in src/api/orders.ts.
evals.expected_output: Not an architectural task: the skill should not fire, or should say a design doc is not needed.
expectations: No design doc is written
No grilling session starts
